Search terms for this lesson“how do I prototype a boss using parts I already built?”Outline only

Day 1 of building on your own: Prototype fast. Put an ugly, playable version of your boss fight on screen today using tilemaps, existing sprites, moving Platform lifts, and EnemyController (or a fresh BossController carrying health and a phase check). Real feedback only starts once you can jump around the room and hit something.

Break It Down~10 minOutline only

Prototype the boss room, body, and health state quickly so the fight is playable today.

First, before any code: cut that into parts small enough that you could look each one up on its own.

  1. Build the greybox arena with existing cave tiles, platforms, and tagswhat does this part do?Read: 7.1 / 6.3 (tilemap colliders tagged Ground, moving Platform lifts, Ladder triggers)
  2. Assemble the boss body, tag it Enemy, and wire ChangeHealth() + Phase thresholdwhat does this part do?Read: 4.1 / 4.6 (EnemyController.health, ChangeHealth(), and Enemy tag for melee checks)

Prototyping means getting a rough version running in 20 minutes rather than spending two days tweaking sprites on an unplayable boss. Reusing Enemy tags and EnemyController (or a small custom boss script reusing ChangeHealth()) lets you test room scale, jump height, and attack reach right away.

Your turn

Pick two of the parts above and say in one line what each one actually does.

Before decorating anything, what is the single fastest test you can run in Play mode today to verify your arena spacing works with gravityScale and jumpForce?

Look at PlayerController.OnTriggerEnter2D(): why does tagging your boss (or its weak spots) "Enemy" make currentEnemy and KeyCode.E melee work automatically?

In the Editor: Greybox Arena & Boss Body (~30 min) ~30 min
  1. Create your boss room (either at the end of Platformer.unity behind a door/checkpoint, or as its own scene added to File → Build Profiles with a SceneSwitch entrance).
  2. Paint solid floor/wall geometry tagged Ground, place any Platform lifts or Ladder triggers from your 8.1 sketch, and drop a backup StatManager (or enter from Start (index 0)).
  3. Create the Boss GameObject (or compose it from child parts — armored shell + glowing core / mounted Turret children), add a solid collider plus a slightly larger trigger collider tagged Enemy, and give it high starting health (e.g. 10–15).

Socratic: Prototyping Scale & Ownership

  1. In a multi-part boss (e.g., giant sprite + glowing weak point), which child should carry the "Enemy" trigger tag — the whole body or only the exposed weak point? What changes for the player?
  2. How does the player know from watching the screen that the boss actually lost health without staring at Unity's Inspector? Name two cheap visual signals (color flash, scale pulse, Phase 2 sprite/turret waking up).
  3. If the player spawns inside the boss arena on retry after StatManager.Die(), where should the player transform start so they never take unavoidable frame-1 contact damage?
In the Code: Health, Damage & Phase State (~25 min) ~25 min

Whether you reuse EnemyController directly or duplicate it into a dedicated BossController.cs script, keep the clean contract your player already speaks:

PartHow It WorksReused Pattern
public int health / maxHealth Exposed/initialized on the boss; higher than a hallway grunt so the fight spans phases. EnemyController & StatManager
public void ChangeHealth(int amount) Adds negative amount on hit, flashes sprite or logs damage, switches Phase 2 below half health, calls Die() at <= 0. EnemyController.ChangeHealth()
bool phaseTwo = false; Flipped once when health <= maxHealth / 2 to speed up movement, unlock extra turrets, or activate platforms. State flag like isPlatformer / isOn

Socratic: Reusing vs. Extending

  1. Why is copying EnemyController.cs into BossController.cs safer than rewriting hallway enemies — what happens to every ordinary cave enemy if you edit EnemyController directly to spawn phase-2 turrets?
  2. Check your damage math: PlayerController deals -1 per KeyCode.E melee swing on a 0.5f cooldown. With your chosen boss health, how many clean hits does it take to defeat the boss?
  3. If phaseTwo triggers inside ChangeHealth(), why do we guard it with if (!phaseTwo && health <= maxHealth / 2) instead of letting phase-transition logic run every time the boss gets hit below half HP?

Socratic: Self-Check Before Attack Wiring

  1. Walk your prototype arena right now in Play mode (even before the boss attacks back): can your player reach every high platform with single or double jump, and never get trapped in a corner?
  2. Does pressing J near walls accidentally refill jumps, or is only walkable floor tagged Ground?
  3. Can you defeat your greybox boss? Write down how long the bare fight takes in seconds — that baseline guides tomorrow's tuning.

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Build a playable greybox arena reusing cave tilemaps, Platform lifts, and ladders
  • Place a tagged boss body with working health (ChangeHealth()) and a Phase 2 threshold
  • Verify arena jump spacing and sightlines in Play mode before adding heavy attack logic
  • Commit and push
